summary.oneLiner: Over five decades, Linc has grown from a writing instruments manufacturer into one of India's most recognised stationery brands.
summary.business: Linc designs, manufactures and sells writing instruments and stationery for students, professionals, institutions and households, spanning mass-market price points through to premium, design-led products. Its owned brands are Linc, Pentonic and Swype, complemented by strategic associations with Mitsubishi Pencil (Uni), Deli and Morris of South Korea. The Company is evolving from a pen company into a broader stationery solutions business and serves customers in more than 40 countries through exports, regional partnerships, joint ventures and local manufacturing.

currentContext.strengths: Brand familiarity built over decades across generations, with extensive availability and a product-value proposition understood at mass-market price points|Design-led premium platform in Pentonic, which by FY2024-25 accounted for approximately 36% of Linc's revenue and has extended across formats, categories and price points|Diversified export footprint across more than 40 countries, reducing concentration risk and dependence on any single geography|Local manufacturing in Kenya through the 60%-owned Gelx, which avoids the 25-35% Common External Tariffs the East African Community imposes on imported finished consumer goods and creates a Made in Africa cost advantage|International product partnerships that pair external product expertise with Linc's own manufacturing and commercial capability - Mitsubishi Pencil, Morris of South Korea, Deli, and the Silka Linc Kirtasiye joint venture in Turkey|Distribution reach across General Trade and Modern Trade, supplemented by growing e-commerce penetration and a digitalised distribution and demand-planning system|Premiumisation of the export basket, led by Pentonic, which improves margins and reinforces positioning in the premium writing instruments segment

Ltd. arrangement with Ondesk Ventures Pvt. Ltd.
currentContext.expansion: The central expansion project is a new manufacturing facility spanning approximately 1.5 lakh square feet, designed to consolidate operations currently spread across multiple locations under a single roof. The immediate gains described are improved operational efficiency, reduced logistical complexity and manufacturing processes that no longer lose time in transition between sites; beyond that, the facility has been designed with future expansion built in, so additional capacity is available when demand asks for it. The Company presents it as a long-term commitment rather than a single project - the physical foundation for its next phase of manufacturing growth. Progress continued on this integrated manufacturing facility during FY2025-26 and the plant is described as still in progress rather than commissioned; no commissioning date, rupee quantum or capacity figure is stated in this bundle. Alongside the plant, investment continued across product innovation, strategic partnerships and distribution: commercial production commenced under the Mitsubishi Pencil India joint venture, the stationery portfolio expanded into adjacent categories, and the Company enhanced its presence across Modern Trade and digital commerce while strengthening its General Trade sales organisation. On the market side, Linc is re-balancing its export portfolio away from geographies hit by geopolitical conflict, tariff shifts, anti-dumping duties and regional instability, placing greater emphasis on Indonesia, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia and South Africa - a re-balancing management is candid will take years, not quarters. Investments were funded from strong operating cash flows, with a net cash position maintained and capacity preserved to support future investments.

risks.risk: Raw-material and freight cost inflation that pricing cannot recover in time
risks.note: Higher costs of polymers, inks, packaging materials and freight placed pressure on margins, and polymer costs increased faster than pricing could be revised. The Company adopted a calibrated pricing approach, absorbing a portion of the increases to protect customer relationships, so cost spikes land on margin rather than on price.

risks.risk: Intense pricing competition in a price-sensitive category
risks.note: FY2025-26 was characterised by intense pricing competition. The Company consciously refrained from participating in unsustainable price-led competition, choosing to preserve brand equity, product quality and profitability - a deliberate choice that trades volume for margin and can cost share if rivals keep discounting.

risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption and trade barriers across export markets
risks.note: Several traditional export geographies were shaken by geopolitical conflict, tariff shifts, anti-dumping duties and regional instability outside the Company's control, and geopolitical uncertainty affected demand across selected export markets.

risks.risk: Concentration in export geographies that are slow to replace
risks.note: The Company is re-balancing toward steadier markets - Indonesia, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia and South Africa - but management is candid that re-balancing an export portfolio takes years, not quarters, so exposure to the older, more volatile geographies persists through the transition.
Corporate sales moderated during FY2025-26 against a strong previous-year base, and softer corporate sales were one of the reasons revenue from operations remained only broadly stable.

risks.risk: Execution risk on the integrated manufacturing facility
risks.note: The new facility, spanning approximately 1.5 lakh square feet, is intended to consolidate operations currently spread across multiple locations under a single roof; it is still described as work in progress, so the promised efficiency, logistics and future-capacity benefits remain contingent on completion, and consolidating multiple sites into one concentrates operations at a single point.

risks.risk: Dependence on partnerships and new platforms that have not yet scaled
risks.note: Growth rests heavily on initiatives still ramping - the Mitsubishi Pencil joint venture, the Turkey partnership, the Morris relationship and the Kenya subsidiary - while Linc On is only expected to contribute meaningfully from FY2026-27 onwards, so near-term earnings carry the investment without the return.

risks.risk: Margin and return-ratio moderation while investment continues
risks.note: Investments across manufacturing, product innovation, strategic partnerships and distribution, together with external headwinds, moderated profitability during the year; net worth improved and a net cash position was maintained, but return ratios moderated in line with profitability even as spending continued.

one-line thesis: Linc Limited reported modest 5.8% revenue growth in Q3FY26 driven by volume expansion (+20% in writing instruments), but margins contracted due to a strategic shift to lower-ASP mass market products and one-time labor regulation costs. While domestic volumes are strong, international JV contributions remain in the investment phase with delayed profitability, capping near-term earnings upside despite a healthy balance sheet.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 129.29 Cr (+5.8% YoY); EBITDA INR 12.9 Cr (10% margin, down from ~10.7% normalized); PAT INR 6.77 Cr (-191 bps YoY); Order Book: Turkish JV 2026 book 'promising' (no specific value); Net Debt: Net Cash INR 10.14 Cr. One-offs: Employee benefit expense spike due to labor regulation changes impacted margin by ~70 bps.
guidance: Revenue growth to accelerate as new products scale; Margins expected to improve over time with shift to >INR 10 segments despite current mass-market mix pressure; Order inflow strong in Turkey; Capex: Bengal facility delayed to Q1FY27.
order book & pipeline: Turkish JV order book for 2026 described as 'quite promising'; no specific numerical value provided for consolidated order book.
segment / subsidiary detail: Writing Instruments volume 16.4 Cr units (+20% YoY); Pentonic volume 6.5 Cr units; Export share stable at ~20%; Marker category launched in 2-3 zones with encouraging response but limited by current capacity constraints.
growth verticals / optionality: Scale-up of Marker category pan-India pending capacity expansion; Monetization of Kenya subsidiary sales momentum; Maturation of Turkish and Mitsubishi JVs to reduce loss drag; Entry into higher price point (>INR 10) segments to lift ASP.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin compressed to 10% (reported) vs 10.7% (normalized) due to product mix shift to INR 5 MRP segment lowering ASP (from INR 6.3 to INR 5.0) and one-time labor regulation costs; JV losses of INR 0.83 Cr further impacted PAT.
capex / expansion: Bengal manufacturing facility (linked to Morris Korea JV) delayed, now expected operational Q1FY27; Gradual capacity scaling for Marker category to support pan-India launch.
capital allocation: Net cash position of INR 10.14 Cr; Focus on organic capacity expansion and JV maturity; Improved cash conversion cycle (61 days vs 63 days FY25).
risks & watch-items: Prolonged JV losses delaying consolidated profitability; Intense competition in mass market segment pressuring ASP; Execution risk on Bengal facility commissioning; Export market uncertainty in East Africa.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'conscious choice' of measured growth over aggressive expansion; Acknowledges delays but stresses foundation building for long-term value.
non-obvious takeaways: Volume growth (+20%) significantly outpaced revenue growth (+5.8%) indicating a deliberate strategic pivot to lower-price high-volume segments to gain market share, temporarily sacrificing realization (ASP dropped to INR 5).

hero.oneLiner: Over five decades, Linc has grown from a writing instruments manufacturer into one of India's most recognised stationery brands.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Over five decades, Linc has grown from a writing instruments manufacturer into one of India's most recognised stationery brands.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Linc designs, manufactures and sells writing instruments and stationery for students, professionals, institutions and households, spanning mass-market price points through to premium, design-led products. Its owned brands are Linc, Pentonic and Swype, complemented by strategic associations with Mitsubishi Pencil (Uni), Deli and Morris of South Korea. The Company is evolving from a pen company into a broader stationery solutions business and serves customers in more than 40 countries through exports, regional partnerships, joint ventures and local manufacturing.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Writing Instruments volume 16.4 Cr units (+20% YoY); Pentonic volume 6.5 Cr units; Export share stable at ~20%; Marker category launched in 2-3 zones with encouraging response but limited by current capacity constraints.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Owned brands:** Linc, Pentonic, Swype
- **Strategic associations:** Uni (Mitsubishi Pencil), Deli, Morris
- **Pentonic family:** BRT, GRT, Compass, mechanical pencils, SF pencils, Evo
- **Legacy / earlier products:** TipTop, Hi School Gel, Smart OBG, Twinn, Linc Touch
- **New product launches, FY2025-26:** Linc brush pen, Pentonic twistick, Linc mech pencil, Pentonic SF pencil, Linc fineliner, Justclick highlighters and markers, Swype highlighters

end_markets.body:

- North America

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Turkish JV order book for 2026 described as 'quite promising'; no specific numerical value provided for consolidated order book.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth to accelerate as new products scale; Margins expected to improve over time with shift to >INR 10 segments despite current mass-market mix pressure; Order inflow strong in Turkey; Capex: Bengal facility delayed to Q1FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Scale-up of Marker category pan-India pending capacity expansion; Monetization of Kenya subsidiary sales momentum; Maturation of Turkish and Mitsubishi JVs to reduce loss drag; Entry into higher price point (>INR 10) segments to lift ASP.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Global writing instrument market valued at USD 47.64 billion in 2025, expected to grow from USD 50.1 billion in 2026 to USD 77.97 billion by 2034 at a 5.69% CAGR, with Asia Pacific holding a 39.77% share in 2024
- Indian writing instruments market valued at USD 858.03 million in 2025 and expected to reach USD 1,070.50 million by 2034, a 2.4% CAGR over 2026-2034; India contributed 5.98% of the global market in 2025
- Pens dominate Indian demand at approximately 65% of the total in 2025, driven by use across educational institutions, offices and households
- Global stationery products market valued at USD 165.87 billion in 2025, rising from USD 173.93 billion in 2026 to USD 268.08 billion by 2034 at a 5.56% CAGR, with Asia Pacific the largest share at 43.17% in 2025
- Demographics: India's population estimated at 1.47 billion as of July 2026 with a significant proportion in the 5-24 age group, and over 65% of the population below 35, forming the core consumer base
- Education spending: the Union Budget FY2026-27 allocated H139,289.48 crore to the Ministry of Education, an 8.27% increase over the FY2025-26 budget estimate, supporting rising enrolment and therefore writing-instrument demand
- Urbanisation: approximately 37.6% of India's population is urban, expected to reach 40% by 2030, driving higher disposable incomes, brand consciousness and preference for premium, aesthetically designed products
- Premiumisation: the luxury writing instruments and stationery market is expected to reach USD 5.43 billion by 2030 at a 4.6% CAGR as consumers seek quality, aesthetics and brand appeal
- Rising literacy: India's literacy rate rose from 74.0% in 2011 to 80.9% in FY2023-24, expanding the base of people in formal education and professional activity
- Joint ventures and strategic collaborations between Indian and international companies are accelerating innovation, product quality and consumer choice in the industry
- Structural headwind: proliferation of smartphones, tablets, styluses and smart learning technologies is gradually reducing reliance on traditional writing tools, while green schooling and digital learning platforms reduce reliance on paper-based materials - offset by the enduring preference for pen-and-paper learning and the cognitive and tactile benefits of handwriting, which are expected to sustain baseline demand
- E-commerce and online platforms are unlocking growth through wider reach, product customisation and premium gifting demand
- Eco-friendly demand: heightened environmental awareness is pushing manufacturers toward recycled or biodegradable alternatives
- Management outlook: the Company is expected to generate profitable and sustainable growth in the foreseeable future

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin compressed to 10% (reported) vs 10.7% (normalized) due to product mix shift to INR 5 MRP segment lowering ASP (from INR 6.3 to INR 5.0) and one-time labor regulation costs; JV losses of INR 0.83 Cr further impacted PAT.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Net cash position of INR 10.14 Cr; Focus on organic capacity expansion and JV maturity; Improved cash conversion cycle (61 days vs 63 days FY25).

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The central expansion project is a new manufacturing facility spanning approximately 1.5 lakh square feet, designed to consolidate operations currently spread across multiple locations under a single roof. The immediate gains described are improved operational efficiency, reduced logistical complexity and manufacturing processes that no longer lose time in transition between sites; beyond that, the facility has been designed with future expansion built in, so additional capacity is available when demand asks for it. The Company presents it as a long-term commitment rather than a single project - the physical foundation for its next phase of manufacturing growth. Progress continued on this integrated manufacturing facility during FY2025-26 and the plant is described as still in progress rather than commissioned; no commissioning date, rupee quantum or capacity figure is stated in this bundle. Alongside the plant, investment continued across product innovation, strategic partnerships and distribution: commercial production commenced under the Mitsubishi Pencil India joint venture, the stationery portfolio expanded into adjacent categories, and the Company enhanced its presence across Modern Trade and digital commerce while strengthening its General Trade sales organisation. On the market side, Linc is re-balancing its export portfolio away from geographies hit by geopolitical conflict, tariff shifts, anti-dumping duties and regional instability, placing greater emphasis on Indonesia, the Philippines, Saudi Arabia and South Africa - a re-balancing management is candid will take years, not quarters. Investments were funded from strong operating cash flows, with a net cash position maintained and capacity preserved to support future investments.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'conscious choice' of measured growth over aggressive expansion; Acknowledges delays but stresses foundation building for long-term value.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Brand familiarity built over decades across generations, with extensive availability and a product-value proposition understood at mass-market price points
- Design-led premium platform in Pentonic, which by FY2024-25 accounted for approximately 36% of Linc's revenue and has extended across formats, categories and price points
- Diversified export footprint across more than 40 countries, reducing concentration risk and dependence on any single geography
- Local manufacturing in Kenya through the 60%-owned Gelx, which avoids the 25-35% Common External Tariffs the East African Community imposes on imported finished consumer goods and creates a Made in Africa cost advantage
- International product partnerships that pair external product expertise with Linc's own manufacturing and commercial capability - Mitsubishi Pencil, Morris of South Korea, Deli, and the Silka Linc Kirtasiye joint venture in Turkey
- Distribution reach across General Trade and Modern Trade, supplemented by growing e-commerce penetration and a digitalised distribution and demand-planning system
- Premiumisation of the export basket, led by Pentonic, which improves margins and reinforces positioning in the premium writing instruments segment

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Prolonged JV losses delaying consolidated profitability; Intense competition in mass market segment pressuring ASP; Execution risk on Bengal facility commissioning; Export market uncertainty in East Africa.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Volume growth (+20%) significantly outpaced revenue growth (+5.8%) indicating a deliberate strategic pivot to lower-price high-volume segments to gain market share, temporarily sacrificing realization (ASP dropped to INR 5).

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen the sustainability framework through greater resource efficiency, safer operations, inclusive employment practices, stronger measurement systems and responsible capital allocation - stated objective is to grow the business without leaving responsibility behind
- Maintain governance discipline as the Company expands across products, markets and partnerships, so that consistency holds across a wider organisation
- Financial prudence as an explicit governance principle: disciplined capital allocation, conservative accounting and Balance Sheet strength
- Data-led control - digital systems …

| Competitive pressure in mass segment | Competitors in Premium Segment | beneficiary | Low | Linc's focus on INR 5 segment may cede premium share temporarily to rivals focusing on >INR 10 SKUs. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
